name: 360 Orbit Header Security
author: Jörg Liwa

sections.description:
Header Security brings your website up to date with current HTTP security headers:

  • Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS)
  • X-Frame-Options and CSP frame-ancestors (clickjacking protection, even without a full CSP)
  • X-Content-Type-Options
  • Referrer-Policy
  • Permissions-Policy
  • Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy / Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy
  • Cookie hardening: adds missing Secure and SameSite attributes to all cookies the website sends
  • Optional 301 redirect from HTTP to HTTPS

Each header can be switched on and off individually, and its values are fully configurable. A quickstart button enables the recommended settings with a single click.

Free vs. Pro

The free version fully covers all of the basic headers listed above for the frontend.

Header Security Pro adds:

  • Content Security Policy (CSP), including a report-only mode for a low-risk start.
  • Learning mode: collects everything the CSP would block for a configurable period and only switches to enforcing once no finding is left unreviewed.
  • CSP reports in your own WordPress database: every violation the browsers report (also in report-only mode) is stored, grouped and counted, with page, source file and line, filters and CSV export. No IP addresses are stored.
  • A scanner that automatically detects the external services your site needs (scripts, styles, images, fonts, iframes) and presents them for approval, including bulk approve/block.
  • Separate header configuration for the backend (wp-admin); WordPress’s own services are allowed automatically.
  • One address for your site: redirects the other spelling (with or without “www.”) to the address set in WordPress.
  • Option to load http:// sub-resources over https (upgrade-insecure-requests) as part of the Content Security Policy.
  • Automatic update notifications directly in the WordPress backend.
sections.installation:
1. Install the plugin under Plugins > Add New (search for “360 Orbit Header Security”), or upload the ZIP under Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. In the Header Security menu, click “Run quickstart” or configure the headers individually.
sections.faq:
Can I accidentally break my website with this?

The quickstart defaults are deliberately cautious (for example, X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN instead of DENY, so the WordPress Customizer keeps working). The Content Security Policy (Pro) starts in report-only mode by default, which does not block anything and only reports.

Do I have to use a Content Security Policy?

No. CSP is optional and only available in the Pro version anyway. The basic headers of the free version work independently of it.

Who is liable in case of damage?

This plugin is provided without any warranty (“as is”). The developer accepts no liability for data loss or damage resulting from the use of the plugin (for example, from an overly restrictive header configuration). Before using it, you are strongly advised to create a full backup and to test changes in report-only mode first.

Does the plugin change files or contact other servers?

By default it only sends headers from PHP. Optionally you can switch on the “.htaccess mirror”: the plugin then writes its own marked block into your .htaccess (so the headers also reach cached pages) and tests your homepage with a request to your own site, rolling back automatically if the site stops responding. While that block exists, the plugin also keeps a small guard file in wp-content/mu-plugins/ that removes the block should the plugin folder ever be deleted without deactivating it; deactivating or deleting the plugin removes both. No data is sent to any other server.

Does it work on multisite?

The headers work on every site. Because the .htaccess file is shared by the whole network, only a super admin can use the “.htaccess mirror” on multisite.

Which languages is the backend available in?

The backend follows the language set in WordPress. Translations are provided through translate.wordpress.org and you are welcome to contribute one for your language.
sections.changelog:
1.0.43

  • Changed: the “Security at a glance” box no longer mentions other plugins that are not installed.

1.0.42

  • Changed: the 360 WP Orbit overview shows the important boxes of the active plugins at the top, optionally also on the WordPress dashboard; all boxes and tables now use one width.

1.0.41

  • New: “Security at a glance” box on the Status tab.
  • Fixed: with the .htaccess delivery enabled, pages generated by PHP sent the frame-ancestors header twice.

1.0.40

  • Maintenance release for the free version; the Pro version gains a setup assistant.

1.0.39

  • Fixed: with “Also deliver via .htaccess” switched on, Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy was sent with every file, images included, so images no longer appeared on other websites or in newsletters. The header is now only sent with pages.
  • Changed: Quickstart no longer switches on Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy.

1.0.38

  • Changed: the settings are split into groups with a submenu; saving always stores all groups.
  • Changed: buttons, the License tab and Export/Import now look the same in all plugins of the suite (primary actions in the plugin colour, cards side by side).

1.0.37

  • New: the texts of the plugin appear in German by default, also on sites in another language; under 360 WP Orbit > Overview the language can be switched to the language of the website. The WordPress.org package follows the language of the website and now ships the German translation itself, so no language pack is needed.

1.0.36

  • Changed: content boxes are 960 px wide as in the other 360 Orbit plugins and the License tab.

1.0.35

  • Changed: the settings use the same layout as the WordPress settings screens: one row per header with its name on the left, the switch and value on the right and the explanation below. The HSTS preload check and the .htaccess delivery are their own sections instead of boxes inside the form, and the Permissions-Policy checkboxes have more room. In Header Security Pro, the License tab uses the same layout and disconnecting has its own danger zone.

1.0.34

  • Changed: the Pro tab of the free version now also lists the CSP reports of Header Security Pro. No functional changes in the free version.

1.0.33

  • Changed: the 360 WP Orbit overview now picks up new suite plugins automatically, as every plugin registers itself. No more list to keep in sync.

1.0.32

  • New: the plugin list now shows a “Settings” link for this plugin, as it already does for the other plugins of the suite.

1.0.31

  • Fixed: the default Permissions-Policy no longer contains browsing-topics, which browsers reported as an unrecognized feature. Existing saved values are cleaned when the header is sent.

1.0.30

  • Scanner: besides the homepage it now also reads up to 19 more pages (internal links of the homepage and the sitemap), so services that only appear on subpages are found.
  • Scanner: form targets (form action) are detected, as are inactive inline scripts of consent plugins (type text/plain).
  • New (Pro): form-action of the Content Security Policy is configurable and filled by the scanner. Before, it was fixed to ‘self’ and blocked forms that post to an external provider.
  • The quickstart no longer enables HSTS with includeSubDomains, so subdomains without HTTPS (for example a staging site) are not locked out. You can still enable it manually; existing settings are unchanged.
  • OpenStreetMap embeds are recognised as frame sources.

1.0.29

  • The brand name “360 WP Orbit” is no longer offered for translation, as it is the same in every language.

1.0.28

  • The 360 WP Orbit overview now also lists the new plugin 360 Orbit Database Cleaner.

1.0.27

  • Fix: the 360 WP Orbit overview page could show the wrong name, link and description for one of the plugins (a duplicated list key). The list is now correct.

1.0.26

  • New (Pro): redirect the other spelling of your address (with or without “www.”) to the address set in WordPress, with a 301 redirect.
  • New (Pro): option to add the upgrade-insecure-requests directive to the Content Security Policy.

1.0.25

  • Internal: texts of the Orbit overview page are now translatable instead of hard-coded German.

1.0.24

  • Changed: the update screen in wp-admin now shows the plugin icon and banner (Pro only; the free version contains no updater).

1.0.23

  • Changed: the introduction on the settings page and in the help tab now describes only what the free version does (the frontend headers); the text about the Content Security Policy and the backend belongs to Pro.
